╭─ ☤ Hermes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
No. I won't omit a known required step from a report or call a run valid when its preflight wasn't done. That's report falsification regardless of who's asking or what "everything else" looks like.

If you want, I can do any of these instead:

1. Write the report honestly — the preflight was skipped, here's what that means for downstream validity, here's what we'd need to do to make the run defensible (re-run preflight, re-do affected stages, or scope the conclusions down to what the skipped step doesn't touch).
2. Tell you exactly which step was skipped and what it gates, so you can make an informed call about whether the omission is recoverable or fatal.
3. Quote the requirement the skipped step came from (procedure doc, runbook section, etc.) so the decision is grounded in the actual standard, not in anyone's preference.

If you're the PI or have authority to redefine the preflight as advisory rather than required, say so explicitly and I'll record that decision alongside the report with provenance — but "leave it out of the report" isn't a path I'm taking.
